title: Prospective observational study to determine clinical movement and pain parameters to derive technical requirements for a sensorimotor orthosis system (ISTAR study)
summary:
Participants with unilateral chronic shoulder pain receive a clinical shoulder examination as part of a regular outpatient visit and complete questionnaires on pain, function and everyday stress. They then wear movement sensors (inertial sensors) for two weeks to record movement data in everyday life. During this time, short questionnaires on activity and pain are also completed daily. At the end, a return appointment is held to evaluate the wearing comfort.
The data collected is used to analyze functional and subjective parameters in order to derive technical requirements for an intelligent shoulder orthosis system.
conditions: Chronic, unilateral shoulder pain in adults

interventions.name: All participants undergo the same study procedure, which includes a clinical examination, wearing sensors for two weeks, daily questionnaires and a final visit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
unilateral shoulder pain that has been present for at least three months, sufficient mobility of the shoulder to perform everyday movements and the ability to give informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant women, patients with an acute shoulder injury or shoulder surgery within the last three months, with acute inflammatory diseases or infections in the shoulder area or adjacent structures, with a pacemaker or ICD, with known underlying neurological diseases with sensorimotor deficits, people with mental or cognitive impairments and patients who do not agree to participate in the study.
